findings.title: Possible TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or null for Google Meet events
findings.body: The code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. If destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (possible when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, as handleNewBooking can set it to null), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and evaluating the Google Meet fallback throws a TypeError, breaking booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video. It should use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Google updateEvent loses destination-calendar fallback
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares externalIds against undefined/null and therefore never matches, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined. Previously it fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined, so updates for bookings without an externalCalendarId on the reference fail instead of updating the destination calendar. The fallback should be the first/matching destination calendar, not a find against the falsy argument.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent loses destination-calendar fallback and may delete from primary
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, the find compares each destination calendar's externalId to that falsy value and returns undefined, so deleteEvent falls back to `primary`. Previously it used the stored destination calendar. Cancelling a booking whose event lives on a non-primary destination calendar will therefore target the wrong calendar (or 404/be silently resolved) and leave the actual event undeleted.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses first host's destination calendar for every host
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar/credential, passing the matching credential, but Office365 (like Lark and CalDAV implementations) ignores the credentialId/externalId argument and uses only `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event with multiple hosts, the second host's credential is used to create an event on the first host's calendar ID, causing 404/authorization failures or a duplicate event on the wrong calendar rather than an event on the second host's calendar. The per-credential destination must be selected by credentialId.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses first host's destination calendar for every host
findings.body: EventManager loops over all destination calendars and creates one event per credential, but Lark's createEvent still derives calendarId solely from `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. A collective booking's additional hosts therefore attempt creation on the organizer's Lark calendar with their own credentials, which fails or writes to the wrong calendar, so the multi-host fix does not work for Lark. It needs to pick the destination whose credentialId matches the credential used for this call.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar, and team calendars are added via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With null, the optional-chain push is a no-op, so for a collective event where only non-organizer hosts have destination calendars, those calendars are lost and EventManager falls back to creating only one event on the first generic calendar credential. Initializing to [] or assigning the team array would preserve them.

findings.title: Non-credential destinations create events without storing externalCalendarId/credentialId correctly
findings.body: In the branch where a destination has no credentialId, createAllCalendarEvents calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing destination.externalId (unlike the credentialId branch at line 370). EventResult.externalId is therefore undefined, and referencesToCreate stores externalCalendarId undefined for that calendar event. Subsequent reschedule/cancel/update operations cannot address the specific external calendar the event was created on and may target primary/the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes the first calendar reference for every credential and repeats per outer reference
findings.body: Inside the new loop over all bookingCalendarReference entries, the recurring branch maps over all organizer calendar credentials and for each updated booking uses `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes('_calendar'))`, i.e. always the first calendar reference regardless of the credential being iterated or the outer reference. With multiple hosts/references this issues duplicate deleteEvent calls with mismatched credential/uid/externalCalendarId pairs, potentially failing to delete some hosts' events and repeatedly deleting others.
